units.translation: raising shrill cries with soul-conducting laments
Thus Blomfield for τριχός δ᾽ ὀρθίας [the hair standing upright]. Of a raised and strained voice.
and the upright lock of hair stands on end
and a shrill echo rang out in response
child of right-counselling Themis, you who sit on high
where Triclinius says: for Zeus struck Asclepius with a thunderbolt for raising Hippolytus.
Zeus put a stop to the rightly skilled one bringing back the dead
for Zeus struck Asclepius with a thunderbolt for raising Hippolytus
making the hair stand on end
making the hair stand on end
he sets his foot upright or covered
do you lift your dear head upright?
and may Agreus Apollo guide the arrow straight
upright witnesses appearing for the dead
Not found elsewhere in the tragedians, but frequent in Hippocrates, on whom see Thes. vol. 5 p. 2182.
standing upright, sleepless, not bending the knee
to raise, set upright; to guide; to establish; to set straight, correct
where Hermann conjectured σαοῖ [may he save], since the strophic verse ends in an iamb.
[The interpolator said this of those acting rightly]
often in troubles he raises the helpless one
a single vote set the house upright
one must stand upright and cast the vote and decide the case
who guides destiny by ancient law
for me who set aright the sword-bearing contests
for the reverent we will set misfortunes upright
now you have set straight the judgment of my mouth
and having erred much, you set nothing right in your mind
for in a messenger a hidden word is set straight
and when things are set upright, we are ever more constant in honoring the city of Pallas
and to Ilium a rightly named alliance drove the wrath that brings fulfillment
it would be rightly and justly named
who indeed rightly perished according to their name, and much-contested
no deceit, unless from my heart I speak rightly
it would be a teacher of the matter rightly
learn how rightly I will speak
count rightly the castings of the votes
to divide; to bound, claim for oneself
and cutting the opposite land in two by fate, she bounds the wavy strait
I claim as my boundary the land of the Perrhaebians and the regions beyond Pindus
and I claim as my boundary a remedy under the stars for a grievous marriage by flight
Explained by grammarians as εἱρκτή [prison], περίφραγμα [enclosure], φραγμός [fence], as indicated in Thes. vol. 5 p. 2198. Of the towers of besiegers which are brought up to the walls.
Thus Casaubon for ὁρκίων αἱρουμένους [taking oaths]. ὁρκίοις αἱρουμένους [taking by oaths] Paleius.
